name: Abu Dhabi

supply.note: Abu Dhabi's potable supply is overwhelmingly desalinated seawater. No annual production mix with a year attached has been captured.

freshness_note: TAQA Distribution's Utility Tariff 2025 dates itself to 1 January 2025 and is what the publisher links today as its full tariff guide. No 2026 edition exists. The 2025 rates page remains the customer-facing statement of the same figures.
awaiting: One question, and it holds the services figure alone: whether a residential wastewater charge is levied on a metered Abu Dhabi household, by whom and at what rate. Separately, an Executive Council or Department of Energy instrument would replace a live publisher schedule with a recorded search over the instruments themselves — tidier provenance for the same rate.
open_items: Whether a residential wastewater charge is levied on a metered Abu Dhabi household, by whom and at what rate. The distributor's own tariff document prices no wastewater tariff for any segment, and its bill guide names Waste Water among the activities a bill can show while giving no rate. This holds Total Water Services and does not touch the supply figure.

Any Executive Council or Department of Energy instrument setting or superseding the residential water tariff since 1 January 2025. Continuity currently rests on the publisher's live schedule, which Rule 3.10 permits.
grade_note: Grade A. Both of the questions that held this city are closed, and neither was closed by a better reading of an ambiguous sentence. The VAT ambiguity fell to an unchanged rate across the introduction of the tax. The recurring-charge question fell to the publisher's own bill guide, where the water service line equals the consumption section's total including VAT exactly — a residual would have been a recurring charge, and there is none.
why_this_is_not_a_missing_document: It was twice, and it is neither now. Precedence could not resolve the VAT sentence — §7.5 ranks a statutory formula above a billing formula above a presentation table, and neither reading of that footnote was a formula — so what resolved it was a second document from the same publisher, four years older than the tax, showing the rate unchanged across its introduction. The recurring charge was a missing document, and a named one, and it arrived: the residential Understand Your Bill guide, which enumerates a bill rather than a schedule. Absence needs an enumeration, and a booklet that prices one fixed charge is not one.
resolution_note: Two conflicts resolved and both kept readable. The VAT record keeps its two candidate bills, AED 117.60 and AED 123.48, and the reason the second governs. The recurring-charge record keeps the seam in its own argument: the specimen bill the absence is read from is a UAE National account, the concessionary class the benchmark excludes, so what is read from it is the format of a bill and not the price of one. Same rule that keeps New York's superseded 13.50 visible beside 13.86.
uwti_note: Grade A and eligible on its own merits. The base basket admits one territory per country and the United Arab Emirates already carries Dubai; which of the two is seated is a decision for the freeze, not a property of this record.
